comment: The shared communication audio service (shared/media/communication-audio.cpp, rungic-communication-audio.service, the provider, on the Linux side) and its consumer, the phone mode's session (agent/assistant/session/audio.cpp). Framing: the Unix socket $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/rungic-communication.sock, JSON lines both ways on one long connection; one owner at a time (another client gets an error and is disconnected; a request before open gets an error too). The owner sends open (its session id, muted), then mute, flush (the playback was interrupted: queued audio of the old epoch is dropped) and close, each with an id the reply carries. The service answers open with ready once Android's communication output, control and (unless muted) microphone are up, and then the PulseAudio devices android_communication (playback) and android_communication_microphone (recording) carry the call's audio; it sends position every 100 ms (Android's played and written frames of the current epoch) and error when the session fails (the owner must resume explicitly). Behind it the service uses the audio contract's communication ops on Android's capture socket. Opening a session switches Android into communication mode, so the provider check on the phone only sees that the service is there and refuses a request without a session. Tested from both ends: tools/system/tests/communication_audio.py (on the Mac mini: the real audio.cpp against a stand-in of the service, and the real service, with a fake pactl, against a client and a stand-in of Android's capture socket) and acceptance scenario contract.communication-audio.
